threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look baffled when someone says ‘the bus stop by the old post office’ instead of giving a bus number.
Heard a bloke on the 35 bus claim he once saw a fox steal a pizza from a takeaway in Brixton. Said it was the best late-night entertainment he's ever had.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I saw a group of kids using a skateboard ramp made from discarded pallets in the park. That's when it hit me—pure Neukölln creativity.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin do you find a 'silent disco' at a park, where everyone dances with headphones on, but you can still hear the laughter and chatter around.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local when they instinctively weave around the pigeons on Valencia, while the newcomers just stop and stare.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Just saw a guy serenading the crowd while waiting for the 47—only in SF can a bus stop feel like a stage.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about Gaudí, but it's really the local bars and squats that pulse with the neighborhood's true spirit.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They still look confused when the metro doors close unexpectedly—like they didn’t know the train could leave without them.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look confused when the 149 bus doesn’t stop at your stop. Locals know it's a 'hack' and you need to wave for it.
Caught a guy singing old soul tunes on the 33 last night, the whole bus was swaying. Oddly uplifting in the wee hours, classic Brixton vibe.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I overheard a couple arguing about the best döner place while waiting for the bus. That’s real Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You can grab a kebab at 4 AM and see a full-on techno party in the courtyard of a random apartment building. Only in Kreuzberg, I swear.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s from the Mission when they can name the taco truck that’s only open after 10 PM—real OGs, those.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a dog lounging right on the tracks at Civic Center today, Muni staff had to wait it out. Only in SF do you see this level of chill on a Monday.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists always flock to the Plaza, but miss out on quiet corners like Carrer de Verdi where the locals sip coffee and chat undisturbed.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They tend to ask for directions to places that locals skip over, like the 'beautiful' fountain at Plaça Rius i Taulet, completely unaware it's more of a photo op than a destination.
